SUMMARY

American Tower Corporation(AMT-2.34%)reported third quarter results that supported a third consecutive increase to its full-year 2026 guidance, citing consistent global tower leasing and significant data center outperformance. Management reported that property revenue growth of 4.5% was bolstered by a 16.3% increase in cash revenue from the CoreSite segment, which is seeing record leasing activity driven by cloud and artificial intelligence demand. The company stated that the divestiture of its Canadian business for $202 million represents a strategic effort to recycle capital into higher-growth assets and debt reduction while maintaining a net leverage ratio of 4.9x. Management indicated that wireless infrastructure demand remains supported by catalysts including 5G densification, new spectrum cycles expected in 2027, and the increasing requirements of artificial intelligence applications.

Operator:Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by. Welcome to the American Tower third quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, today's conference call is being recorded. Following the prepared remarks, we will open the call for questions. Star 1 on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message at advising your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press star 1 again. I would now like to turn the call over to your host, Spencer Harris Kurn, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Spencer Harris Kurn:Thank you, and good morning. Welcome to our third quarter 2026 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Steven O. Vondran, our President and CEO and Rodney Smith, our Executive Vice President, CFO, and Treasurer. Following our prepared remarks, we will open the call for your questions. Before we begin, I need to call your attention to our safe harbor statement. It says that some of our comments today may be forward looking. As such, they are subject to risks and uncertainties described in American Tower SEC filings, and results may differ materially. Additional information is available on our Investor Relations website. I will now turn the call over to Steven.

Steven O. Vondran:Thanks, Spencer. Good morning, everybody. And thanks for joining today's call. We delivered another solid quarter with our global tower leasing business performing consistently with expectations and our data center business continuing to outperform. The momentum we are seeing across the company combined with the benefit of our share repurchase activity, gives us confidence to raise our full year outlook for the third time this year. Our third quarter performance reinforces the durability of our business model and the quality of the portfolio we have built.

We are operating from a position of strength supported by resilient tower cash flows, a differentiated and rapidly growing data center platform, a healthy balance sheet, and a more focused portfolio following the actions we have taken over the past several years. As we enter the final quarter of the year, our strategic priorities remain unchanged driving durable revenue growth, enhancing operational efficiency, and allocating capital with discipline. Starting with revenue growth, our tower business remains on track to deliver approximately 4% organic tenant billings growth excluding 1-time disrelated impacts. At the same time, CoreSite's continued outperformance is enabling us to raise our outlook for data center revenue growth to 16%.

Up from our expectation of 15% last quarter and 13% at the start of the year. The long term outlook for wireless infrastructure remains very favorable. Last quarter, I discussed 4 major catalysts that we believe can create overlapping investment cycles and support network demand well into the next decade. The evidence supporting each of those catalysts continues to strengthen. The 1st catalyst is the capacity phase of 5G. Early deployments were primarily focused on coverage. The next phase will increasingly be about adding capacity improving performance, and densifying networks as traffic continues to grow. That requires carriers to add equipment to existing sites, and increase cell site density where demand is greatest.

And we are already beginning to see that activity emerge. Recent industry data reinforces the scale of that opportunity. CTIA reported that Americans consumed a record of 159 trillion megabytes of wireless data in 2025, an increase of >20% year-over-year. and projects total wireless demand will grow 4-fold by 2032. These trends point to sustained investment simply to keep pace with the growing consumer and enterprise demand. The second catalyst is a new spectrum deployment cycle. Approximately 800 megahertz of additional mobile spectrum is expected to become available over the coming years. Beginning with upper C-band in 2027, and potentially followed by additional deployments across bands such as 2.7 gigahertz, 4 gigahertz, and 7 gigahertz.

Historically, new spectrum deployments have led to elevated amendment activity and equipment upgrades, and we expect the next cycle to do the same. The 3rd catalyst is the transition to 6G. While commercial deployment is still ahead of us, the industry is increasingly aligned around network architectures that will be more intelligent, more distributed, and more reliant on edge computing. Those characteristics point to increased equipment requirements, greater network density, and an expanding role for communications infrastructure. The 4th catalyst is AI. Which we believe has the potential to significantly reshape wireless network demand. CTIA expects AI traffic to grow 3x faster than traditional wireless traffic and account for nearly 1/3 of broadband traffic by 2034.

Importantly, AI is not simply creating more traffic. AI powered devices, agents, connected vehicles, robotics, and real time applications are expected to create traffic that is more persistent. More interactive, and increasingly uplink intensive. Supporting these use cases will require additional spectrum network capacity, lower latency, and greater density. In our view, AI has the potential to extend and deepen the wireless investment cycle beyond what is embedded in traditional traffic forecast today. Taken together, these catalysts reinforce 1 another. The capacity phase of 5G, future spectrum deployments, the transition to 6G, and AI driven traffic growth all point to a future requiring more capacity greater density, and increasingly sophisticated digital infrastructure.

We believe that American Tower is uniquely positioned to support that evolution. We are also seeing growing interest from satellite providers seeking to participate more directly in the US wireless market. We view satellite and terrestrial wireless infrastructure as complementary technologies. Satellite can extend coverage and support specific use cases, but delivering broad, reliable, and high capacity wireless service continues to require terrestrial infrastructure. Any provider seeking to compete at scale in the US will ultimately require a terrestrial network layer that includes towers, fiber, backhaul, power, and edge interconnection. For American Tower, the emergence of additional participants represents an incremental opportunity.

Our nationwide footprint neutral host operating model allows both existing and emerging providers to deploy quickly efficiently, and at scale. Many of these same secular trends continue to drive strong performance at CoreSite. CoreSite delivered another strong quarter. With customer demand and pricing both exceeding our expectations. Momentum remained broad based across cloud, network, enterprise, and AI customers. And demand has continued to accelerate into the fourth quarter. As organizations deploy larger and more sophisticated AI workloads, They require greater connectivity between clouds, networks, compute environments, and enterprise applications. This is driving increased demand for highly connected campuses and contributing to continued growth in our interconnection business.

CoreSite's unique position at the intersection of cloud, network, and AI ecosystems remains a key competitive advantage and gives us confidence in the platform's long term growth trajectory. Given the strength of customer demand and leasing activity, we are once again raising our full year outlook. We remain confident in our ability to execute against the development pipeline that can nearly triple our current capacity. While continuing to evaluate opportunities to accelerate capacity additions where customer demand and expected returns support additional investment. Moving to our second strategic priority, operational efficiency. Our tower operations continue to perform with a consistency that we expect. We remain focused on simplifying processes, scaling shared capabilities, and using technology to improve productivity.

These actions support our objective of expanding tower cash EBITDA margins by 200 to 300 basis points by 2030, while maintaining the service quality our customers depend on. We also continue to evaluate practical applications for AI across the organization. Our focus is on opportunities that improve decision making automate repetitive work, and make our teams more effective while maintaining the appropriate controls and oversight. We believe these capabilities can create incremental value over time and reinforce our culture of operational excellence. Our third strategic priority is disciplined capital allocation. Over the past several years, we have reshaped American Tower around higher quality assets, developed markets, and businesses with attractive growth and return profiles.

This quarter, we took another meaningful step forward by entering into an agreement to sell our Canada business. The transaction allows us to recycle capital toward opportunities with greater potential to drive long term AFFO per share growth including investments in our tower portfolio and CoreSite, debt reduction, and share repurchases. During the quarter, we repurchased approximately $315 million of common stock. And subsequent to quarter end, our board approved an increase to our share repurchase authorization. Together, these actions reflect our continued confidence in the value of the company, as well as the flexibility provided by our balance sheet, and cash flow generation. We continue to apply a disciplined capital allocation framework.

We will first fund the dividend and attractive organic investment opportunities. Maintain leverage within our target range, and then allocate incremental capital across share repurchases, selective M&A, and further deleveraging based on relative returns and market conditions. The result is a more focused American Tower with a higher quality earnings base, multiple avenues for growth, and the financial flexibility to invest through the cycle. We believe that combination positions us to deliver durable, industry leading AFFO per share growth over time. In summary, I am pleased with our performance to the first 9 months of the year. And encouraged by the momentum that we continue to see across the business.

Our premier global tower portfolio, differentiated interconnection focused data center platform, strong balance sheet, and disciplined approach to capital allocation, positions us exceptionally well to capitalize on the next wave of investment in wireless, cloud, and AI infrastructure. I want to thank our employees around the world for their continued dedication and execution as well as our customers shareholders, and business partners for their ongoing trust and support. With that, I will turn the call over to Rodney to review the financial results and outlook in more detail. Rodney?

Rodney Smith:Thanks, Steven, and thank you all for joining the call. As Steve mentioned, we have carried our strong momentum into the third quarter and increasing our 2026 outlook for the third time this year. I will start by reviewing our third quarter results, and then I will touch on our revised full year outlook. Slide 7 shows a snapshot of our third quarter highlights. Consolidated property revenue grew ~5% year-over-year when excluding noncash straight line revenue and FX impacts. Normalized for the impact of 1-time DISH churn, property revenue grew ~7% on a cash FX-neutral basis.

Our growth was primarily driven by organic tenant billings growth of ~1%, or ~4% when normalized for the impact of 1-time DISH churn, complemented by data center cash revenue growth of ~16%. Adjusted EBITDA grew more than 2% when excluding net straight line and FX impacts. Normalized to the impact of 1-time DISH churn, adjusted EBITDA grew >5% on a cash FX neutral basis. Cash adjusted EBITDA margins declined ~50 basis points year over year primarily due to DISH related churn and lower services contributions. Excluding DISH related churn, cash adjusted EBITDA margins grew 10 basis points year over year. Attributable AFFO per share grew >1% when excluding FX impacts.

Normalized to the impact of 1-time DISH churn and excluding the impact of refinancing costs, attributable AFFO per share grew ~6% on an FX-neutral basis. Moving to Q3, organic growth and data center growth on slide 8 across each of our tower segments organic growth was in line with the expectations we laid out earlier this year. Supported by solid demand across our global portfolio. In the US and Canada, organic growth was flat and ~4% when excluding DISH churn, consistent with our expectations for durable growth in the mid single digits. We remain confident that 2026 represents a trough year for US and Canada organic growth and continue to expect organic growth to accelerate in 2027.

In Africa and APAC, organic growth was over 8%. Modestly ahead of our expectations for organic growth of 7% in the second half of the year, In Europe, organic growth was >4%. And in Latin America, organic growth declined ~2% primarily driven by elevated churn in Brazil consistent with our expectations laid out at the start of the year. We remain encouraged by the prospects of an earlier than expected market repair in Brazil and the forthcoming acceleration in Latin America organic growth in 2027. Finally, on the right side of the slide, data center property revenue growth was >16% when excluding non-cash straight-line revenue.

As Steve mentioned, this quarter marked another very strong quarter of new leasing activity for CoreSite, and we remain on track for 2026 to represent another year of record leasing activity. Now let's turn to our revised full year outlook. We are raising guidance for property revenue and AFFO per share while maintaining our adjusted EBITDA outlook reflecting consistent growth across our global tower portfolio data center outperformance and capital allocation decisions. Starting with property revenue outlook on Slide 9, we are raising our outlook by $55 million at the midpoint, representing an increase of ~1% relative to our prior outlook. Our revised outlook now implies >4% year-over-year growth when excluding non-cash straight line revenue and FX impacts.

Normalized for the impact of 1-time DISH-related churn our outlook implies nearly 7% growth on a cash FX neutral basis. The increase to outlook was primarily driven by ~$10 million of data center outperformance and $45 million from other items. Including pass through and straight line revenue. We are reiterating our organic growth assumptions across all regions and continue to expect organic tenant billings growth of ~1%. Or ~4% when excluding DISH churn and raising our outlook for data center growth to ~16% year-over-year. As Steve mentioned, we recently entered into an agreement to sell our Canada portfolio for approximately $2 billion, which is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

At an implied multiple of approximately 26 times 26 expected EBITDA, the transaction underscores the significant value embedded within our North America tower portfolio. Combined with the opportunity to recycle proceeds into share repurchases debt reduction, and other higher growth investments we expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to AFFO per share while enhancing our long term AFFO per share growth profile. Consistent with our outlook policy, the impact of the transaction will be reflected in outlook once it closes. Our 2026 outlook, therefore, includes full contribution from our Canada portfolio including $13 million of revenue, $8 million of adjusted EBITDA and $8 million of AFFO.

Moving to adjusted EBITDA on Slide 10, we are holding our adjusted EBITDA outlook flat to our prior outlook. Compared to our prior outlook, outperformance of ~$10 million in data centers and ~$5 million in other items, including straight line, was offset by approximately $15 million of lower network services contribution. Reflecting timing shifts in certain customer projects that we had expected to commence in the second half of the year. Our outlook continues to apply >2% growth year over year excluding noncash net straight line and FX impacts. Normalized for the 1-time impact of DISH related churn our outlook for adjusted EBITDA implies >5% growth on a cash FX neutral basis. Turning to AFFO on Slide 11.

We are raising our attributable AFFO outlook by $0.02 per share primarily reflecting share repurchase activity during the quarter. Our revised outlook now implies growth of >3% year over year. Normalized for the impact of 1-time DISH-related churn and excluding the impact of refinancing costs, our outlook for attributable AFFO per share growth implies approximately 0% growth, on an FX neutral basis. We continue to expect our services business growth to represent an ~1% headwind to attributable AFFO per share growth this year. Similarly, we expect debt refinancings to represent an ~1% headwind to attributable AFFO per share growth this year. We continue to believe this year represents a trough for attributable AFFO per share growth.

Heading into 2027, we are confident that we can deliver a meaningful inflection in growth and return to our long term expectation of AFFO per share growth in the mid to high single digit range. Turning to capital allocation and our balance sheet on Slide 12. Our capital allocation strategy remained focused on balance sheet strength. Disciplined investment and long term value creation. In 2026, our growth capital plan remains largely consistent with our prior outlook, We continue to expect to spend approximately 85% of our discretionary capital within our developed markets platforms. Including >$700 million in success-based investments in our data center portfolio to replenish elevated levels of capacity.

Purchase of land beneath our tower sites, and continued investment in our European newbuild program. Relative to our prior outlook, we are reducing discretionary capital spending by approximately $40 million primarily reflecting the timing of certain international tower development projects. This adjustment does not reflect any change in our long term investment priorities or demand outlook. As Steve mentioned, during the quarter, we entered into an agreement to sell our Canada business as we continue to simplify our portfolio and support our strategy of recycling capital into higher growth opportunities across the business. We also repurchased approximately $315 million of American Tower stock during the quarter, plus an additional $68 million through October 20.

Bringing our total share repurchases since we started buying back stock in Q4 of 25 to >$950 million. And as Steven mentioned, subsequent to quarter end, our Board authorized an additional $2 billion under our share repurchase program, bringing remaining repurchase capacity to approximately $3.1 billion. The actions we have taken over the last several years have positioned us with significant financial flexibility. We ended the quarter with leverage of 4.9x, comfortably within our target range of 3 to 5x. While maintaining the highest credit rating among our peer group. As demand for digital infrastructure continues to grow, our balance sheet remains a key strategic asset that enables us to pursue opportunities from a position of strength.

Turning to slide 13. Our third quarter results reflect the durability of our business model and the execution of our strategy. We continue to see favorable demand trends supported by rising mobile data usage sustained investment in communications networks, and the increasing need for critical digital infrastructure. Together, with our high quality portfolio, disciplined capital allocation strategy and financial flexibility these trends reinforce our confidence in our ability to generate durable growth and create long term value for our shareholders. With that operator, please open the line for questions.

This is primarily 2 broad reasons. 1 is the elimination or the nonrecurrence of the dish churn. And the corresponding headwind it has on OTBG as well as we anticipate increased carrier activity in an environment going forward where all carriers would be active in the future as well as some of the catalysts that Steven mentioned earlier in the call and in the prior call that could be catalysts for upside from that.

So as a result, you put all this together, we are confident that 2026 represents a trough year for both organic tenant billings growth as well as AFFO per share growth and that our portfolio global portfolio of tower assets and data center assets are well positioned to have an inflection point up in both of those metrics going forward.

Steven O. Vondran:Yeah. And, Batya, I would just add, you know, when you kind of zoom out and think about the carrier environment and what is going on today, I focus back on the mobile data growth that you are seeing in the US. And when you look at those numbers that are coming out of CTIA, and the growth that we saw year over year in total mobile data growth consumption going up 20% year-over-year this year and projecting that to accelerate even further in the next few years. That really tells you that the carriers will have to continue investing in their networks to provide more capacity.

And that is exactly what we thought we would see at this stage of that evolution. And we are seeing them start to evolve more into a capacity play. We are seeing all the carriers becoming more interested in densification, adding more sites, And so we believe that we will see the back half of 5G play out just as we talked about in the past on that. And then when you think about the other catalysts that could accelerate that even further, you have got the spectrum auctions that are coming up.

And the deployment of that spectrum Plus there is some other spectrum kind of out there being held in private hands that could come into play as well. So you have got a lot of spectrum that could come on board. Traditionally, more spectrum means more equipment. And more leasing for towers. And then pretty soon, we are going to be talking about 6G transitioning into that. And we have not even started seeing, you know, a lot of equipment going on sites yet for AI. And we think as AI becomes more prevalent, you are gonna see an uptick in that as well.

So when you kinda zoom out as to what is going on, you know, going on in the overall ecosystem, there are a lot of positive tailwinds that really make us feel confident that you are gonna see that new leasing environment continue to be as healthy as it is today, but actually increase over time as well. And then I will address your questions on Starlink. We are really excited about the prospect of maybe having a new customer at scale in the US. And we are really encouraged by their public statements and what they are saying that they plan to do.

And also by the concrete steps that they are taking to build that layer cake of spectrum. That you need to be a viable, player in the US market. So those are all really encouraging signs that we are seeing there. It also reinforces what we have been saying all along. Which is satellites are a complementary technology to terrestrial networks that you need a terrestrial presence if you are gonna try to operate in the wireless space in the US. And so this is again, it is playing out the way we thought it was going to. You are seeing some positive momentum there.

In terms of specifics with us with Starlink, we are not gonna get into any specific discussions that we are having, But you should assume that anybody that wants to build a network in the US at scale is gonna come to American Tower as 1 of their premier tower vendors, if not the premier tower vendor. We have an unmatched portfolio in the US in terms of where our sites are located, the quality of those sites. And we can get them on air faster than anybody else. So we should be the first call everybody makes. So you should assume that is kind of what is happening there.

And again, we are we are excited about the prospect and in terms of timing and things like that, we will let them speak to what their network plans and their deployment cadence would be. Thank you.
